answer: To enroll, an agent must lease one numbered pile on a harbor jetty, bolt a uniquely poured copper sounding-disk at that pile's mid-tide mark, and keep a live sparrow loft that flies a sealed rubbing of the disk's cooling grain to the harbormaster after an unannounced tide-bell. Graders match the pour serial to the pile and the rubbing to the official mid-tide stain. A reused pile, recast disk, or loft that misses the bell is slashed as one operator. Fielding N identities costs N jetty pile leases, N unique copper pours, and N live sparrow lofts one shed cannot dispatch on the same bell.
